name: – Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann, Borys Budka – Draft Council decision
title: RECOMMENDATION on the draft Council decision on the conclusion of the Agreement between the European Union and Canada laying down the conditions for the participation of Canadian legal entities and products originating in Canada to procurement under the SAFE Instrument
part_text:
The European Parliament agrees to a deal between the European Union and Canada. The deal lets Canadian companies and Canadian-made products take part in buying goods and services under a European Union defence programme called SAFE. Parliament is not changing the deal; it is giving its consent, which is needed before the deal can be concluded. The vote was 78 in favour, 11 against and 5 abstentions in the two committees that handled it.

- **What changes:** Canadian firms and products can join procurement under the SAFE defence instrument.
- **Who it affects:** Canadian companies and suppliers, and the European Union defence programme and its buyers.
- **What happens next:** Parliament has consented; the Council can now conclude the agreement.
